summary: Stevens County, WA: 1938 pole lookout on Chewelah Peak, replaced 1963 by a timber tower sold and moved to a farm north of Chewelah in 1985.

facts.design: 50-ft pole tower with L-4 cab (1938); 41-ft treated timber tower with R-6 flattop cab (1963)
facts.status_note: The 1963 tower was sold and moved to a private farm north of Chewelah in 1985; the association lists the original summit tower as gone

access.note: The 1963 tower went to a private farm in 1985; no source describes access to the summit today

events.note: A 1925 Colville Examiner item, quoted by WillhiteWeb, mentions a fire warden at the lookout station on Chewelah Peak; its link to the 1938 tower is unknown
50-ft pole tower with L-4 cab, the first tower of the 1938 development
FireLookout.com lists Rachel Butte as lookout for 1945-1950; the list of staff runs to 1977
41-ft treated timber tower with R-6 flattop cab replaced the pole tower
Forest Service staffed the lookout into the 1970s
Washington Department of Natural Resources staffed it for a couple of seasons in the early 1980s
Sold to Frank Scranton and moved to his farm alongside Highway 395, just north of Chewelah

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and WillhiteWeb date the pole tower to 1938, while WillhiteWeb also quotes a 1925 newspaper item about a lookout station and cabin on the peak. The story uses 1938 for the tower and reports 1925 as an unresolved earlier station.

notes_for_editor: The 1938 and 1963 dates and the 1985 sale and move agree across the register, FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb; the register, FireLookout.com and the relocated list say the same things in similar words, so they may share a source. The 1925 cabin item conflicts with the register's 'originally developed in 1938'. WillhiteWeb's 1936 USGS benchmark note (no lookout yet) and 1943 'USFS lookout tower over the station mark' were not used. The register spells the agency 'National Resources' (sic); the story uses 'Natural Resources'. The 'where it stands today' line is undated. The Chewelah Independent column has no publication date in the text retrieved, but its anniversary headings ('120 Years Ago - August 3, 1906', '80 Years Ago - August 1, 1946') point to 2026, so it is the most recent source found for the Scranton move; it is not a site visit or photo, so the tower's condition is still unconfirmed. No new photos added; the register photos are already on the parent record.
